rationale: This is a horizon-lengthened clone of the archived PhysicalTiltGrossProfitMiss (same two legs, TREND(3) substituted for DELTA(1)), a cosmetic variant of an already-strong signal rather than a new mechanism.

Sits squarely on top of the archived MoatFragileCapexLumpiness (same capex-volatility gate with a reshuffled second leg), and the R&D-intensity volatility term is degenerate for the large mass of COALESCE-to-zero non-R&D firms, so the "instability" leg largely proxies for R&D reporting status.

A coherent and genuinely new pairing — gross-capacity expansion gated on inventory build versus R&D improvement — that is a recombination of archived ingredients but not a duplicate of any single prior signal (CapacityBuildDemandOptionGap used sales productivity, not inventory), with sign and expression consistent.

Identical in structure and hypothesis to the archived RDSpendSellThroughValidation with only GROWTH(sale) swapped for DELTA(gross profit/at); the swap is not motivated by any diagnosis of that signal's fmb/alpha disagreement and reads as a one-term cosmetic edit.

Recombines the exact ingredients of the archived CapexAfterGoodwillDrawdown (which already showed a wrong-signed fmb_tstat of +3.36), and the leading gate is mechanically degenerate because COALESCE(gdwl,0) leaves most firms with a zero delta and tied ranks, so the multiplicative conditioning does little real work.

The hypothesis is a near-verbatim restatement of the archived EquityFinancedRDNotEmpireBuilding with two terms shuffled into the use-of-proceeds spread, offering incremental noise rather than a distinct economic mechanism.
